studentAssets.observations: Graph of f'(x): an upward-opening y-axis-symmetric parabola with vertex (0,-1), meeting the horizontal ray y=2 at x=1; the derivative is constant at 2 to the right of x=1.

independentAnswers.studentFacts: f is continuous; its derivative graph is the symmetric quadratic segment and line shown; f(2)=3; ask f(-1)f(3). Choices -3,-2,0,2,5.
independentDerivation: The parabola has vertex (0,-1) and passes through (1,2), so its equation on x<=1 is f'(x)=3x^2-1; for x>=1 the graph gives f'(x)=2.
Integral from -1 to 1 of (3x^2-1) dx is 0, and integral from 1 to 2 of 2 dx is 2. Thus f(2)-f(-1)=2, so f(-1)=1.
f(3)-f(2)=integral from 2 to 3 of 2 dx=2, so f(3)=5.

independentAnswers.studentFacts: A monic quartic f is even; it has a local maximum value 4 at x=0 and local minima at x=-2 and x=2; find f(x) and f(3).
independentDerivation: Even monic quartic has form f(x)=x^4+bx^2+c.
f(0)=4 gives c=4. Also f'(x)=4x^3+2bx=2x(2x^2+b); critical points at ±2 require b=-8.
Check: f''(x)=12x^2-16, so f''(0)=-16<0 and f''(±2)=32>0, matching the stated extrema.
